t.E160d.agn: In 2008 EFSA set an ADI of 0.5 mg/kg body weight/day for lycopene from all sources, based on an increase in a liver enzyme (ALT) seen in a one-year rat study. In 2009 JECFA allocated an ADI 'not specified'; in 2010 EFSA explained that this difference arose from a different interpretation of the same study. In EFSA's 2026 exposure assessment, natural lycopene in foods, additive use and novel food use were calculated together; in the most realistic scenario, intake in high-consuming infants reached 0.97 mg/kg per day, and the largest source of total intake was lycopene naturally present in foods.
t.E160d.found.0: Flavoured fermented milk products and processed cheese
t.E160d.found.1: Confectionery and chewing gum (up to 300 mg/kg in chewing gum)
t.E160d.found.2: Fine bakery wares, snacks, soups and sauces
t.E160d.found.4: Meat product casings and decorations, surimi and fish pastes
t.E160d.prod: Lycopene can be obtained by chemical synthesis, by extraction from tomatoes or from fungal biomass.
t.E160d.regx.0: ADI from all sources 0.5 mg/kg body weight/day.
t.E160d.regx.1: Total exposure from natural foods, additive and novel food sources was assessed.
t.E160d.summary: A red pigment found in tomatoes. Gives a red colour; used in drinks, sauces and desserts.
t.E160d.what: The carotenoid pigment that gives tomatoes their red colour; used as a red colour.
